summary: Said Reza Huseini specializes in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at King's College London, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and Leiden University (~2017–2021).

Saiyid Athar Abbas Rizvi (1921–1994) worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University and under Mohammad Habib, later holding posts at Jammu and Kashmir, SOAS, JNU, and the Australian National University.
Sakda Hemthep works in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed an MPhil at Cardiff University by 2014, studying under supervisor Max Deeg.

Sakunoshin Motoda (1862–1928) was a scholar in religious studies and other fields. He studied at Kenyon College, the University of Pennsylvania, and Columbia University, later serving at Rikkyo University from around 1899 to 1923.
Sakutaro Fujioka (1870–1910) specialized in Japanology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1891–1894) and later held a post there from around 1900 to 1910.

Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga (b. 1945) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under teachers including Khenpo Appey and Tenzin Gyatso, founded the Sakya Centre, and served as Abbot of Sakya Monastery until 2017.

Sakyong Mipham (b. 1962) is a religious and Buddhist studies figure. He studied at Oxford, Namdroling Monastery, and under teachers including Chögyam Trungpa and Dilgo Khyentse, later serving on the board of Naropa University until 2018.

Sallie B. King (b. 1952) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religion. She studied under Leon Hurvitz at the University of British Columbia (~1971–1975) and served as Professor of Philosophy and Religion at James Madison University (~1990–2017).

Sally J. Sutherland Goldman specializes in Indology and linguistics. She studied under Shivram Dattatray Joshi and Shrinivasa Shastri, earned her PhD at UC Berkeley in 1979, and later held academic posts there.
Sally McAra works in Buddhist and religious studies. She completed an MA at the University of Auckland (1999–2000), studying under supervisors Christine Dureau and Karen Nero.

Sally Mellick Cutler specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford by 1993 and served as manager of the Pali Text Society Office (attested 1996–1997).

Salomon Lefmann (1831–1912) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Münster, Heidelberg, Berlin (under Franz Bopp), and Paris, before serving as an associate and honorary professor at the University of Heidelberg from 1866 onward.

Sam van Schaik (b. 1972) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Manchester and studied under Lama Jampa Thaye, later holding posts at SOAS and the British Library.
Samani Pratibha Pragya works in religious studies and Indology. She earned a PhD at SOAS University of London, where she was attested as a research assistant in 2020.

Samdhong Rinpoche (b. 1939) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Drepung and Gyuto monasteries and served as Chief Editor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies from 1971 to 2001.

Samten Gyaltsen Karmay (b. 1936) is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Drepung Monastery and the University of London under David Snellgrove, later holding posts at SOAS, Collège de France, and CNRS.

Samuel Beal (1825–1889) was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. A graduate of Trinity College, Cambridge, he examined Chinese Buddhist books for the India Office Library and became Professor of Chinese at University College London in 1877.

Samuel George Frederick Brandon (1907–1971) was a religious studies and history scholar. He studied at the University of Leeds (~1930–1934) and held a post at the University of Manchester from around 1951 to 1971.
Samuel Johnson (1709–1784) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He was educated at King Edward VI School, King Edward VI College, Stourbridge, and Pembroke College.
Samuel M. Grupper is a scholar of Central Asian studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Indiana University, where he studied under Irving Yucheng Lo and Philip West.
